research_input.frequency: FREQUENCY.md rank 20 of 42, moderate; gap number 2 in the reader's own topic list. Sub-topics: Data Streams vs Data Firehose vs Video Streams; SQS vs Kinesis; streaming ingestion; ordering and replay; delivering logs to S3. Pairs: SQS vs Kinesis Data Streams (ordering per shard, replay, several consumers); Kinesis Data Streams vs Data Firehose (custom real-time consumers vs managed near-real-time delivery to S3, Redshift, OpenSearch); MSK vs Kinesis (existing Kafka). Stem signals: 'real-time' vs 'near real-time'; 'LEAST operational overhead' points to Firehose over custom code. Planning input only, never evidence.
research_input.freshness: FRESHNESS.md: Kinesis Data Firehose renamed Amazon Data Firehose 2024-02-09; Iceberg destination GA 2024-09-30; KDS records up to 10 MiB 2025-10-28 (default stays 1 MiB, 1 MB/s per shard unchanged); KDS On-demand Advantage 2025-11-04 (data prices at least 60% lower); KDS delivers directly to S3 2026-08-29 (after 2026-07-15: not examinable yet); Kinesis Data Analytics for SQL fully shut down 2026-01-27 (Managed Service for Apache Flink is the successor); MSK Express brokers and Kafka 4.x (KRaft only) 2025. Found at plan, not in FRESHNESS: KDS default shard quota 20,000 in three Regions 2025-04-21; KDS up to 50 EFO consumers in On-demand Advantage 2025-11-20; on-demand write limit raised 1 GB/s (2023-03-01), 2 GB/s (2023-10-30), 10 GB/s (2024-11-20); cross-account Lambda via resource policy 2023-11-22; warm-throughput scale-down 2026-07-24, dry run 2026-09-01 and service-managed partition keys 2026-09-23 (all not examinable yet); Firehose MSK source 2023-09-26, zero buffering 2023-12-26, Secrets Manager 2024-06-06, S3 Tables 2025-03-14; MSK Express GA 2024-11-07, KRaft for new clusters 2024-05-29, multi-VPC private connectivity 2023-04-28, ZooKeeper to KRaft in-place migration 2026-08-10 and Express data delivery to S3 2026-07-30 (both not examinable yet).
research_input.naming: Current AWS names: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams, Amazon Data Firehose (formerly Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose; the book may say this once), Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (Amazon MSK), Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink (formerly Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics). A Firehose stream was earlier called a delivery stream. Kinesis Video Streams is a card in chapter 36; mention only to tell it apart.
research_input.level: Kinesis Data Streams and Data Firehose are medium depth; MSK is a recognise-only service card (2-services.md) per the registry cards list.
research_input.story: STARTUP.md chapter 34 (stage 4, month 26): Callvale Live starts; up to 3,000 calls live at once; 1,500 events a second at peak, each about 1 KB; two consumers read every event independently (live-insights Lambda alerts the agent within 3 seconds; the other stores events for analytics); events of one call must stay in order; a consumer must be able to read the last 6 hours again. Decision: one SQS queue for each consumer / Kinesis Data Streams with Data Firehose (chosen) / Amazon MSK. Accepts capacity planning and uneven load between shards. Ben asks 'Why not SQS? We already know it.' MSK weighed, not chosen (the team has no Kafka skills). Names: stream live-events, function live-insights, bucket callvale-lake, Fargate service live-ingest. Story numbers are story data, never facts.
